Exercise A

Strange and Wonderful

Read the text. Choose the correct word for each gap.

Before you read — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking — you can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Reading text

Australia has some of the strangest animals in the world, and many of them live nowhere else.

Kangaroos and koalas are marsupials. A baby marsupial is very small when it is born, and it grows in a 1 on its mother's tummy. A baby kangaroo is called a joey.

Koalas are not bears. They eat only eucalyptus 2, and they sleep 18 to 20 hours a day because this food gives them very little energy.

The platypus is even stranger. It is a mammal, but it lays 3. It has a bill like a duck, and the male has a venomous spike on its back legs.

Wombats are famous for their cube-shaped poo. They use it to 4 their area. The emu is a big bird that cannot fly, but it can 5 at up to 50 kilometres an hour.

Some animals are dangerous. Saltwater crocodiles are the biggest reptiles in the world, and in summer, box jellyfish make swimming in the north of Australia 6.

Exercise D

Writing: An Email to Melbourne

Your exchange partner in Melbourne asks: "Which Australian animal do you want to see when you visit me?" Write an email of 6–8 sentences. Say which animal, what is special about it, and why you want to see it.

Plan your text

• Which animal do you choose?

• What is special about it? Use facts from the text.

• Why do you want to see it? Where could you see it?

You can use these: Hi ..., thanks for your email. I really want to see a ... It's an animal which ... I think it's amazing because ... See you soon!
Your text
Aim for 6–8 sentences (at least 30 words).
